title: What If All the Ice on Earth Melted?

scenes.text: What if all the ice on Earth melted? The map you know would stop being the map.
Sea level would rise about 216 feet, around 65 meters. That is taller than a twenty-story building.
The Atlantic coast, Florida and the Gulf Coast would vanish. London, Venice and the Netherlands would go under.
In Asia, all of Bangladesh and land home to hundreds of millions of people would be flooded.
But relax. Scientists say melting every last bit of ice would take more than five thousand years.
Most of that water is locked in Antarctica, which holds about four-fifths of Earth's ice. The ocean is already creeping up.

description:
What if all the ice on Earth melted?
